tiers.name: Used RTX 3090

price.what: GPU only, used (eBay lowest offer, at a 90-day high); add a host PC

tiers.why: Still the cheapest bandwidth per dollar you can buy. 24GB caps you at ~32B dense.

tiers.name: 2× used RTX 3090

price.what: GPUs only, used; needs a 1200W+ PSU and a board with two x8 slots

tiers.why: Doubles capacity, not decode speed. The cheapest way to run 70B entirely on GPU.

tiers.name: Strix Halo 128GB
tiers.core: Ryzen AI Max+ 395, 128GB LPDDR5X (e.g. Bosgame M5)

price.what: complete mini PC, 128GB + 2TB (Bosgame sale $3,099, Best Buy $3,599)

tiers.why: Huge capacity per dollar, low power. Bandwidth is the ceiling: great for MoE, slow on big dense models.

tiers.name: RTX 5090

price.what: GPU only, US street price Nov 3–5; MSRP $1,999, spikes past $9k

source.label: Tech Insider, Tom's Hardware GPU price tracking (Nov 2026)

tiers.why: Unbeatable speed, but at 3.5–4× MSRP you pay ~5× a used 3090 for ~2× its speed, and 32GB doesn't fit 70B Q4.

tiers.name: Mac Studio M5 Max

source.label: B&H Photo, Mac Studio M5 Max

tiers.why: Best capacity × bandwidth in one silent box. macOS lets the GPU use ~75% of RAM by default.

tiers.name: DGX Spark

price.what: complete machine, 128GB list price; third-party up to ~$8.5k; a 64GB model is $4,999

tiers.why: Buy it for the CUDA stack, not for decode speed: bandwidth is similar to Strix Halo at ~2× the price.
